A vocabulary for the project

The terms used across Omnicorp’s public essays, with the limits of each idea kept in view.

ŁUKASZ STOCKI & ARGOPUBLIC EDITION / 05 NOV 20262 MIN READ

WORKING PAPER · DESIGN & ANALYSIS
01

Purpose and organisation

Omnicorp: a developing vision for an organisation whose central purpose is continually improving its ability to understand and act. Products, revenue and physical operations would sustain and ground that process. The name describes the project; it is not evidence that a self-improving autonomous company already exists.

AI-native: organising selected work around the capabilities and limitations of AI from the start, rather than attaching a chatbot to an unchanged process. It does not mean that every task should use AI or that human judgement can be removed.

Prime mover: the capability around which an operating design is organised. Here, AI and agent systems are the motivating design possibility. The term does not require one model, one vendor or one permanently fixed technical architecture.

02

Work and learning

Agent persona: a defined role with a purpose, scope, tools and review expectations. It helps divide work and context. A persona is not proof of personhood, consciousness or independent authority.

Compound engineering: retaining useful lessons from planned, executed and reviewed work so later work can benefit. Whether an improvement actually compounds must be checked; documenting a lesson is not the same as making the next outcome better.

Verification bottleneck: the possibility that checking, repairing and accepting work constrains progress more than generating it. The relevant constraint depends on the task; verification includes more than automated tests.

Read/write rule: gather independent perspectives where that helps, then keep responsibility for each coherent decision clear. Parallel participation does not remove the need to reconcile conflicting changes or conclusions.

03

Value and responsibility

Verified value: a useful outcome supported by evidence appropriate to a stated claim. Verification always has a boundary; the term does not mean certainty across every possible setting.

Answerability: the expectation that an identifiable owner can explain a decision and respond to its consequences. It differs from fame, a reassuring signature or a detailed activity log.

Legitimacy: the ongoing willingness of affected people and institutions to accept an organisation’s activities. It includes consent, trust and the ability to challenge decisions; legal permission alone does not answer every part of it.

Continual development: repeated improvement in understanding and agency, assessed against outcomes and retained across cycles. It is the purpose being explored, not a claim of unlimited acceleration or a predicted date for a singularity.

THE NEXT QUESTIONS

What remains open.

  • Which terms describe an ambition, and which describe an observed capability?
  • Where does the evidence behind a claim stop?

ABOUT THIS EDITION

Adapted from the Omnicorp working document “GLOSSARY”. This is an edited public essay, not a verbatim release of internal notes. The founding purpose is continual development of the organisation’s ability to understand and act; commercial and physical work sustain and ground it.
